cmd:
[pscustomobject]@{
  Control_CC6_1_Encryption              = (Get-BitLockerVolume -MountPoint C:).VolumeStatus
  Control_CC6_8_DefenderEnabled         = (Get-MpComputerStatus).AntivirusEnabled
  Control_CC6_1_ScreenLockTimeoutSeconds = (Get-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\Control Panel\Desktop' -Name ScreenSaveTimeOut).ScreenSaveTimeOut
  Control_CC6_1_FailedLogonCount        = (Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security';Id=4625} -MaxEvents 20).Count
  Control_CC6_3_LocalAdmins             = (Get-LocalGroupMember -Group Administrators).Name
} | ConvertTo-Json
citation: module 04 §5.4 worked example (byte canon); ConvertTo-Json surface per Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/convertto-json)
notes: Canon JSON shape = the module's §5.4 block and the committed lab bundles (2-space indent, inline arrays). Real PS 5.1 ConvertTo-Json emits 4-space indentation and exploded arrays — matches neither canon source; the module itself labels its output representative (DESIGN-INPUTS fidelity note 2). Collection-semantics property access keeps LocalAdmins an array, as the lab's happy-path evaluator requires.
